name: parse_repo_spec
title: Parse a remote git repo specification

origin.description: Parse the shorthand form of a remote git repository.
origin.details: The shorthand is an optional package name, a username and repository, an optional subdirectory, and at most one of #pull, @ref, or @*release. A package name matches [[:alpha:]][[:alnum:].]*[[:alnum:]]. The subdirectory may end with one slash, so foo/bar/baz/ and foo/bar/baz are equal. Anything else stops with Invalid git repo specification: '<repo>'.
origin.value: A list with package, username, repo, subdir, ref, pull, and release. A member the shorthand omits is an empty string.
origin.example:
parse_repo_spec("metacran/crandb")
parse_repo_spec("jimhester/covr#47")        ## pull request
parse_repo_spec("jeroen/curl@v0.9.3")       ## specific tag
parse_repo_spec("tidyverse/dplyr@*release") ## shorthand for latest release
parse_repo_spec("r-lib/remotes@550a3c7d3f9e1493a2ba") ## commit SHA
parse_repo_spec("igraph=igraph/rigraph") ## Different package name from repo name

translation.description: Parse the shorthand form of a remote git repository.
translation.details: The shorthand is an optional package name, a username and repository, an optional subdirectory, and at most one of #pull, @ref, or @*release. A package name is a letter, then letters, digits, or dots, and it ends with a letter or digit. The subdirectory may end with one slash, so foo/bar/baz/ and foo/bar/baz are equal. Anything else raises Invalid git repo specification: '<repo>'.
translation.value: A dict with package, username, repo, subdir, ref, pull, and release. A member the shorthand omits is an empty string.
